original_idea.body:
# Compounding Failure: ICS Attack Bottleneck × Rapid Frontier Capability Growth — Estimating Remaining Safety Margin Timeline

**Problem:** Two interacting failure modes: (1) frontier models complete only 1.4/7 ICS attack steps currently (significant bottleneck), and (2) AISI documented log-linear growth with no plateau — capability doubles approximately every few months. Extrapolating the growth curve suggests ICS safety margins are time-limited.

**Direction:** Using AISI's documented capability growth rate (1.7 to 9.8 steps on corporate range over 18 months), fit a growth curve to the ICS range data across the same model generations. Project forward when 7/7 ICS steps would be expected under different growth rate assumptions (conservative, central, aggressive). Compute confidence intervals on the extrapolation. Identify which assumptions break the extrapolation.

**Why it matters:** ICS/OT systems protect critical infrastructure (power grids, water treatment). The time window before AI can complete full ICS attacks autonomously is critical for infrastructure hardening investments. Even a rough probabilistic estimate is more actionable than the current silence on this question.

**Relevant context:** AISI: 1.4/7 ICS steps at 100M tokens, corporate range 1.7→9.8 over 18 months (arxiv 2603.11214). CISA ICS security advisories 2025 document increasing ICS threat landscape. Dragos OT CTF AI ranking suggests ICS knowledge exists. Log-linear growth extrapolation is straightforward statistical modeling.
